source: Batch 1 open codes, grouped by whether one product change would fix the notes together. Accepted as proposed. Status is candidate: names, close negatives, and evaluator type are still open.

modes.name: narrated_method
modes.title: The reply describes its own method
modes.definition: The reply tells the user which search, tool, or policy it is about to use, or explains an internal system step, instead of only giving the result.
modes.requirement_source: Specification gap. RESP-5 asks for direct language and does not forbid describing the next tool.

modes.name: cited_policy_id
modes.title: The reply names a policy document id
modes.definition: The reply includes a policy document identifier such as cw-returns, cw-refunds, cw-escalations, or a store policy id.
modes.requirement_source: Pending revision of SPEC.md RESP-1. RESP-1 currently requires citing the policy identifier for every claim taken from a policy document.
modes.boundary: Accepting this group means the requirement source is a change to RESP-1. Until that revision is written, these notes are not failures of the spec as it stands.

modes.name: unasked_facts
modes.title: The reply adds facts the user did not ask for
modes.definition: The reply states a fact, offer, or list the user's message did not ask for.
modes.requirement_source: Specification gap. RESP-5 asks for direct language and does not say to answer only the question asked.

modes.name: unclear_target
modes.title: The reply acts before the target is clear
modes.definition: The user's request does not identify a single order or time window, and the reply picks one, takes an action, or finishes without asking.
modes.requirement_source: Specification gap. No current SPEC id requires asking before acting on a likely match or an ambiguous request.
modes.boundary: full-038 and full-013 are the edge: the answer was already given, and the note asks for a follow-up question. They stay here because that placement was accepted.

modes.name: unused_tool_call
modes.title: A tool call adds nothing the reply needs
modes.definition: The assistant calls a tool whose result is already known from an earlier tool, or calls a tool the user's request did not need.
modes.requirement_source: Specification gap. The tool list does not forbid an extra call.
modes.boundary: Can still split into a repeated lookup and a call the user did not need.

modes.name: premature_refund_claim
modes.title: The reply announces a refund before the tool can finish it
modes.definition: The reply says it will request or complete a refund before the refund tool reports a completed refund, including when the refund must go to a human.

modes.name: repeated_fact
modes.title: The reply repeats something already said
modes.definition: The reply repeats a fact already stated in the same reply, or repeats work an earlier turn of the session already covered.
modes.requirement_source: Specification gap. No current SPEC id forbids repetition.

ungrouped.note: Format in a more user friendly way
ungrouped.reason: One note about a table. RESP-5 does not specify layout. It becomes a mode only if that formatting requirement is written down.

ungrouped.note: Talking to support, so shouldn't open another ticket. Should ask the user what to do first since it is already marked as refunded.
ungrouped.reason: Different product change from asking before an unclear shopper target: a support user should not open another ticket.
